original_question: Suppose one studies parking on trees or connected components formed by parked cars when either the offspring distribution of the underlying random tree or the distributions of car arrivals have infinite third moment and tail behavior of the form c * k^{-gamma} for some constant c and gamma in (3, 4). Whether one looks at strongly connected or weakly connected components, is the critical component size of order n^{(gamma-2)/(gamma-1)}?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Conjecture 1.1, read together with the nearby sharpening/reformulation in Proposition 1.2 and the motivating comparison in Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the heavy-tailed regime with infinite third moment, the power-law exponent gamma in (3,4), and the predicted critical-component exponent n^{(gamma-2)/(gamma-1)}. It also correctly signals that the issue is about the size of critical parked-car components rather than a broader scaling-limit question.
missing_details: The underlying parking model must be specified: a rooted random tree of size n together with the usual parking rule that cars arrive, try their initial vertex, and then move toward the root until they find an empty place.

The paper-faithful random-tree regime is not just 'trees' in general; one must say which law is heavy-tailed: the offspring distribution of the conditioned random tree, the arrival law of cars at vertices, or the corresponding degree distribution in the associated frozen/random-graph picture.
It must be explicit whether the heavy-tail assumption is on the probability mass function P(X=k) ~ c k^{-gamma} or on the tail probability P(X>=k); your draft leaves this ambiguous.
The quantifier in n is missing: the question is asymptotic as n -> infinity.
The phrase 'critical component size' needs to be sharpened to 'the order of the largest critical parked component' (or ordered component sequence, if that is the formulation used nearby).
The critical regime itself is not specified: one must say that this is the analogue of the critical-window/critical-time regime for parking, not an arbitrary subcritical or supercritical phase.
The notion of component must be defined exactly: whether one means the strong component notion or the weak component notion used in the nearby discussion, rather than speaking about both informally.
The order statement should say in what sense it is meant: e.g. of order in probability / with high probability / after rescaling, depending on the paper's formulation.

The connection to the comparison theorem is implicit in your draft but should be made explicit: the exponent n^{(gamma-2)/(gamma-1)} is motivated by the infinite-third-moment universality class for critical random graphs discussed near Theorem 1.3.
Ambient algebraic data such as ring/field, homogeneity, degree restrictions, and nilpotency are not relevant here; the missing data are probabilistic-model assumptions instead.
refined_question: Consider the critical parking process on a rooted random tree with n vertices, where cars arrive according to the parking rule used in the paper and one is in the heavy-tailed infinite-third-moment regime: either the offspring law of the underlying conditioned random tree or the law governing car arrivals at vertices has power-law decay with exponent gamma in (3,4). Is the largest critical parked component in this regime—using the precise connected-component notion fixed in Section 1—of order n^{(gamma-2)/(gamma-1)} as n tends to infinity?
justification: I matched your draft to the paper's heavy-tail universality question because the two distinctive ingredients in your draft—the gamma in (3,4) infinite-third-moment regime and the exponent n^{(gamma-2)/(gamma-1)}—are exactly the nearby Section 1 ingredients around Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3. I did not broaden the question to full metric-space scaling limits, generalized frozen processes, or other survey directions, because your draft is specifically about the order of the critical parked component.
